_comment: Routing-coverage ratchet seeds (road-to-routing-assurance 0.3). Coverage ratio = corpus cases / routed units, per scope, seeded at the MEASURED current value on 2026-08-25. CI fails only on a decrease -- the COUNT-ratchet disposition of lint_trigger_precision.ts. TWO scopes and never one aggregate: a blended figure would read ~0.46 and describe neither surface. Lowering a seed is a defect, not a fix: a ratio falls when a corpus case is removed OR when units are added without cases, and both are things to repair rather than to record.

measurement.rules: intersection of tests/eval/routing-matrix/*.yaml stems with the tier_1+tier_2 ids in dist/router.json, over that id count. Intersection rather than the file count, so a fixture naming no routed rule cannot raise the ratio.

seed_provenance.skills: 123 of 299 skills carry evals/triggers.json on 2026-10-09; was 119 on 2026-10-07, 118 after the third growth of 2026-10-06, 115 after the second growth that day, 114 earlier that day, 112 on 2026-10-04, 111 on 2026-10-02, 107 on 2026-10-01, 103 earlier that day, 102 on 2026-09-30, 101 on 2026-09-19 and 100 on 2026-08-30.
seed_provenance.finding: The gap between the two seeds IS the roadmap defect D1, quantified. The rules surface is ~90% covered by a deterministic corpus that can fail a PR; the skills surface -- the one production routes on -- is far lower and is covered only by a harness that is advisory only, never gating (rule_trigger_eval.ts:4). The figure is deliberately not restated here (corrected 2026-10-01): it read `25%` against a seed that had since moved to 0.3445, which is the same count-drift this file's own history entries keep repairing one field away. The live value is `seed.skills`, two keys above.

road-to-corpus-refresh-cadence-shape step 1.2a authored one corpus file for `accessibility-auditor` (102 -> 103 of 299). Same shape as the 2026-09-30 entry and for the same reason: that step re-checked the skill's grounding corpus against WCAG 2.2 and the APG, which edited src/skills/accessibility-auditor/data/, and check_routing_coverage requires a corpus for every skill a diff touches. Ten cases -- five exemplars including the German phrasing the skill's own description names, three near-misses -- tailwind-engineer for token-level contrast and ui-component-architect for landmarks and heading order, both named in that skill's SKILL.md, plus existing-ui-audit for component inventory, which it does not name and which is included because it runs first over the same surface -- and two counterexamples, one guarding the 'accessible' homonym. The seed rises so the gain cannot be given back silently; it may never be LOWERED. The trigger-corpus holdout pin is re-taken in the same change -- and this growth moves it for the first time on the HOLDOUT side (18 -> 19), because sha256('accessibility-auditor')[0:2] is 0x2f = 47, below the ceiling of 51. That is recorded in the holdout artefact with its ordering claim explicitly scoped to the 18 originally sealed rows. The two published measurements the 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-30 entries name -- routing-body-signal-verdict.json and the measure_delivery_sets record -- are deliberately NOT re-taken here, and the departure from those two entries is stated rather than left to be noticed. The reason is the partition, not the date: this growth is HOLDOUT-side, so the train input both measurements read is byte-identical to what it was before this change -- all 84 train rows reproduce -- and re-taking them would publish the same measurement under a newer date, which is a freshness claim nothing earned. The two artefacts are NOT in the same state, and conflating them would repeat the error this sentence replaces: routing-body-signal-verdict.json carries `corpus.partition: train` and `train_corpora: 84` and is current for the train partition; delivery-set-result-2026-08-31.md still reads `82 train corpora, 764 distinct prompts` and carries no re-take section for either the 2026-09-19 or the 2026-09-30 growth, so it is two corpora stale and those two entries' claim that it `is re-taken in the same change` is not backed by the tree. Repairing it is a train-side measurement re-run, out of scope for a holdout-side growth, and is named here so the gap is attributed rather than inherited silently. A FUTURE train-side growth owes both re-takes. Separately, TWO entries were removed from trigger_eval_grandfather.json, and the two reds are of different kinds. `ui-component-architect` was red ON MAIN: it gained a corpus on 2026-09-30 and its now-false allowlist entry was not removed then, which is the convention the 2026-09-19 entry sets and the 2026-09-30 entry omitted. `accessibility-auditor` was NOT red on main -- on main it ships no corpus at all, and check_trigger_eval_presence fires only on an allowlist entry whose skill HAS one, so its entry went stale the moment this change added the corpus. That red is created here and removed here, in the same change. Stated separately because a reader auditing why two entries were dropped would otherwise be told one pre-existing condition explains both.

Each file carries three positives including one German, two near-misses and one counterexample, with the case class declared per query because that discipline is forward-only and these are added files; the near-misses are the surfaces one step either side rather than easy negatives. The seed rises so the gain cannot be given back silently; it may never be LOWERED. Four entries were removed from trigger_eval_grandfather.json (196 -> 192), none of them red on main beforehand: the gate fires only on an allowlist entry whose skill HAS a corpus, so all four went stale the moment this change added one, and each red is created and removed in the same change. The partition split is 3 holdout / 1 train by name hash, which is why BOTH published train-side measurements the 2026-09-19 entry names are re-taken here rather than skipped the way the holdout-only growth above skipped them: routing-body-signal-verdict.json and delivery-set-measurement-2026-08-31.json both move, and the holdout pin gains three sealed rows plus a new set hash with its ordering claim explicitly NOT extended to them.
